feature: A snap that is showing is a snap you get
summary: Snapping no longer chatters. A line you can see now keeps whatever you are dragging until you have clearly pulled away from it, so landing on a guide is something you do rather than something you catch. Holding Command still drops every magnet, and now keeps them off until you let go of the mouse.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to switch on. Open any screenshot for the caliper steps; a blank canvas with two rectangles is enough for the layer steps.

try.do: Open a screenshot, press I for Measure, and click two feet across something to place a caliper.
Press V, click the caliper, then drag one foot slowly across the picture with a hand that is not steady.
Stop with the yellow guide showing and jiggle the mouse a couple of points either way. The foot should stay on the line.
Keep pulling away until it lets go. Note how far you had to travel before it did.
On a blank canvas draw two rectangles, select one and drag its right edge slowly onto the other one's left edge.
Do it again holding Command: no guide should appear at any point.
Drag a whole layer up the canvas until it centres, and wobble on the centre line.

evaluate: When the yellow line is showing, does the edge look like it is actually ON it rather than near it?
Is the distance you have to travel to shake a line off right, or does it feel like the snap is clinging?
When a snap lets go, is the jump to the pointer acceptable, or does the edge appear to leap?
Does Command staying off for the rest of the drag feel right, or would you expect the magnets back the moment you release the key?
Dragging a foot across a busy screenshot, does it now feel like it is stepping from edge to edge rather than shimmering?
rough: Measured in the real app with two new scripted walks that shake the pointer as they go (Scripts/playtest/snap-hold-walk.json, snap-hold-foot-walk.json). Dragging a caliper foot across the settings capture: before, the guides changed 67 times and went back on a line they had just left 39 times; after, 4 changes and 0 reversals. A layer edge walked onto a neighbour: 6 changes and 2 reversals before, 2 and 0 after. A whole layer moved onto the canvas centre: 4 and 1 before, 1 and 0 after.

The escape distance doubled as a direct consequence: a caught line now lets go at 16 screen points rather than 8, so pulling deliberately away means a slightly bigger jump when it finally releases. That is the trade the fix is made of and the thing to judge.
Command keeping snapping off for the rest of the drag is new. If a reflex Command press mid-drag (for undo, say) makes a drag go free unexpectedly, that will be why.
The screenshots are real screen captures: the probe held the Screen Recording grant for this run.

The old axis gate, which stopped a straight up-and-down drag flashing vertical guides, flipped its own mind near its threshold and was part of the chatter. It now has a wide dead band and keeps its decision while the travel is ambiguous, so it can no longer toggle.
Not covered by the walks: releasing Command in the middle of a drag. A synthesized drag holds its modifiers for the whole gesture, so that half of the rule is only covered by a unit test.
